questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why rock music is more popular than pop
How streaming is changing the way pop songs are made
Why people have stopped buying music
How radio DJs choose which new songs to play on their shows
questions.why: They discuss how music producers are adapting songs for modern technology like streaming.

questions.q: Why does Neil prefer streaming music?
options: It is easier and you can listen anywhere
The sound quality is better than CDs
It is completely free
He can talk over the songs
questions.why: Neil says there are no CDs to buy and load, and it's easier and you can play it anywhere.

questions.q: What have researchers found about pop songs?
options: They are getting longer every year
They use far more instruments than songs did in the past
Long instrumental intros have almost disappeared
Most of them are now written for films
questions.why: Neil says long instrumental introductions to pop songs have become 'almost extinct'.

questions.q: According to Brendan Williams, why are radio playlists important?
options: They help a song make money
They decide which songs win prizes
They let listeners choose songs
They are the only way to hear new music
questions.why: He says radio playlists are important in judging success and feed into a track's commercial success.

questions.q: What happens on Spotify if a song is played for less than 30 seconds?
options: The song is removed from the service
The listener has to pay for it
It is moved to a playlist
It is not counted as a play
questions.why: Brendan Williams says if a track isn't played for at least 30 seconds, it doesn't register a play.

questions.q: What is the aim of getting to the vocals and chorus quickly?
options: To make songs cheaper to record
To keep people listening to the song
To give DJs more time to talk
To make songs easier to dance to
questions.why: The theory is that if we don't hear the vocals, we might not carry on listening.

questions.q: Why does Rob mention radio DJs in the old days?
options: To explain why songs used to be shorter
To say that DJs chose the best songs
To show intros were once useful for DJs to talk over
To complain that modern radio DJs talk far too much between songs
questions.why: Rob says DJs 'loved to talk over that bit', meaning the instrumental intro.

questions.q: Which song does Rob choose as a favourite catchy song?
options: Despacito
Gangnam Style
A rock song with loud vocals
Happy by Pharrell Williams
questions.why: Rob says 'It's got to be Happy by Pharrell Williams. A very catchy song.'
